clue.text: People targeted success with outspoken composer

parts.note: a hit is a success, as in a chart hit

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the composer's name counts by its sound

parts.note: Franz Liszt, the Hungarian pianist-composer, whose surname is said like an inventory of names

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to have scored a success alongside a famously frank musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outspoken' signals that LISZT is only heard, giving LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A roster of intended victims is a phrase for the people someone has marked down to attack.

clue.text: Jack accompanying prophet on leaving, heading north for pilgrimage

indicators.note: in a down light, going north means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack

indicators.note: the word on is leaving, so it is taken out of the prophet's name

parts.note: Jonah, the Old Testament prophet swallowed by a great fish
the word on is taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor travels with a prophet who sets off northward on a holy journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes ON out of JONAH to leave JAH; J plus JAH reads JJAH, and 'heading north' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muslim journey to Mecca that every able believer should make once is this pilgrimage.

clue.text: Novel design of Nazareth among records

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit among the records, so they go inside that word

parts.note: tapes are recordings

indicators.note: a design here is a new arrangement, so the letters of the phrase are reshaped

explanation.surface: A fresh layout for Nazareth found among old records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new but is the noun, a book; 'design' is the anagram signal and 'among' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Rice Burroughs's 1912 jungle adventure book is a novel.

clue.text: Beautiful compositions — fifty framed by clever princess, then put up

indicators.note: in a down clue putting something up means writing it from the bottom upwards
the fifty sits within the word for clever, as a picture sits within its frame

parts.note: sly means cunning or clever
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
Di, Princess Diana

explanation.surface: Pretty poems about fifty pictures, framed by a clever princess and hung on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'framed by' is the container signal and 'put up' turns everything upwards, as this is a down light. Princess here is the crossword's usual Di.
explanation.definitionFit: Idylls are short pastoral poems or scenes of rural charm, the kind of pieces Tennyson wrote of the king.

clue.text: Material inspiring country music player, scenes of domestic violence?

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the material takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: terry is a looped towelling fabric
Oman, the Gulf state
a DJ, or disc jockey, plays music

explanation.surface: Fabric that inspires a country-music performer, then a hint of rows at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country music player' looks like one phrase but splits into a nation and a disc jockey; 'inspiring' (breathing in) holds them.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon cat and mouse spend each episode battering one another around the house, a playful picture of household mayhem.

clue.text: See 22
That Conservative woman

parts.note: her is a word referring to a woman

explanation.surface: Pointing out one particular Tory lady.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: Margaret Thatcher was the Conservative woman prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Thatcher, Britain's first female prime minister, led the Conservative Party from 1975 to 1990.

clue.text: Piece of data in plant, confirmed

indicators.note: the piece of data is placed in the plant's name

parts.note: a reed is a tall waterside grass
a stat is one statistic, a single figure

explanation.surface: A single figure, recorded at a factory, has been verified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory but is the reed.
explanation.definitionFit: To restate a claim is to say it again, so something restated has been reaffirmed or confirmed.

clue.text: Outstanding leader in intelligence, M, noting subterfuge?

definitions.text: Outstanding leader in intelligence, M, noting subterfuge?

parts.note: stellar means outstanding, of star quality

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter
subterfuge is trickery, so the letters are deceptively rearranged

explanation.surface: A brilliant spy chief, known as M, watching out for trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subterfuge' rearranges NOTING to INGTON. As a whole, the clue describes the woman herself: she ran MI5 and inspired Judi Dench's M in the Bond films.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Stella Rimington was the first woman director-general of MI5, Britain's domestic security service.

clue.text: Initially, Khrushchev and Lenin both, unfortunately, failing

indicators.note: things going unfortunately have gone awry, so the letters are jumbled
initially points to the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Two Soviet leaders who both, sadly, fell short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges LENIN BOTH into ONTHEBLIN; the K from 'Initially, Khrushchev' ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a machine that is malfunctioning or failing to work properly.

clue.text: See 4
Financial assessment that's most malicious, restricting good man

indicators.note: the longer word restricts, or holds in, the shorter

parts.note: meanest means most spiteful
ST, saint, is the crossword good man

explanation.surface: A money audit that's especially cruel, keeping a good person under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricting' is the container signal; the good man is the crossword's usual saint.
explanation.definitionFit: A check on someone's income and savings decides whether they qualify for state benefits.

clue.text: I advance with fool past amateur soldiers, as a gunner

indicators.note: the following words come past, or after, the amateur soldiers

parts.note: TA, the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
to advance money is to lend it
a charlie is a fool

explanation.surface: A soldier boasts of lending money and joining a buffoon beyond the volunteers, all as an artilleryman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'past' places the rest after the volunteer reserve. 'gunner' suggests artillery, but this one rode in a bomber's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: RAF slang for the rear gunner of a bomber, sitting at the tail of the aircraft.

clue.text: Eat seconds with squad, carrying last of dinner towards the mouth?

parts.note: to down food is to eat it quickly

indicators.note: the squad carries the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a team is a squad

indicators.note: the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A team wolfing down second helpings, fork heading for the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts R, from 'last of dinner', inside TEAM. The definition plays on mouth as a river's estuary, not a diner's.
explanation.definitionFit: A river flows seaward to its mouth, so going with the current heads that way.

clue.text: Old violin player, say, a member of the orchestra

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: O for old, then a bow, the stick that plays a violin

explanation.surface: An elderly violinist turns out to be one of the orchestral players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violin player' is not a violinist but the bow drawn across the strings.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-reed woodwind instrument found in every symphony orchestra.

clue.text: Intelligent British farmer finally feeding agricultural crop

indicators.note: the inserted letters feed into the crop, going inside it

parts.note: cereal is a grain crop such as wheat

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A clever British farmer at last feeds his grain fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feeding' puts B and R inside CEREAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebral means of the brain, hence intellectual and thoughtful.

clue.text: Inner circle curving inward around line

indicators.note: the curving word wraps around the line

parts.note: concave describes a surface that curves inward

explanation.surface: A tight-knit group bending inward around one line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts L inside CONCAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed, private meeting of insiders, like the cardinals gathered to elect a pope.

clue.text: Expedition to see David Beckham, for example, with centre parting?

indicators.note: the centre parting removes the middle letter of the word, as a parting splits hair down the middle

parts.note: the footballer is a famous celebrity

explanation.surface: A trip to meet the footballer, sporting his latest hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with centre parting' takes out B, the middle letter of CELEBRITY. 'Expedition' looks like a journey but means speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition can mean promptness or speed, a synonym of swiftness.

clue.text: Having recalled iron in the end, I start to remember another metal element

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the assembled letters run backwards
the end of the word is its last letter

parts.note: the ego is the self, the I

indicators.note: the start of the next word is its first letter

parts.note: tin is a metal besides iron

explanation.surface: Remembering iron at last, someone thinks of another metallic element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having recalled' turns the whole assembly round, giving NEGORTIN backwards. 'metal' misleads: the answer is a gas.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaseous chemical element that makes up most of the air.

clue.text: Some parliamentary conclusion by minister?

indicators.note: some of the word, its letters lying inside it

explanation.surface: Part of the closing words of a parliamentary debate.
explanation.walkthrough: The minister is a church minister, ending a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word said at the end of a prayer or hymn, which a clergyman would close with.

clue.text: Happen to break rules as an artist

indicators.note: breaking into a word means going inside it

parts.note: to run a country is to rule it
be can mean take place, as in the party will be on Friday

explanation.surface: A painter who happens to flout the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to break' is the container signal; 'rules' is a verb, as in running a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Paul Rubens was the Flemish Baroque painter.

clue.text: Port some passed on the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the letters are read backwards
some of the words, the letters lying inside them

explanation.surface: Port that some guests passed round the table in the wrong direction.
explanation.walkthrough: Port looks like the after-dinner drink, which etiquette passes to the left; it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: A Black Sea harbour city in Ukraine.

clue.text: Shocking clanger, diet ultimately messed up — by this?

definitions.text: Shocking clanger, diet ultimately messed up — by this?

indicators.note: shocking here means appalling, so the letters are thrown into disorder
ultimately points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dieter's terrible blunder, wrecking the regime with a stodgy dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' rearranges CLANGER, DIET, D (from 'ultimately messed') and UP. A clanger is also a British suet pudding, so the whole clue paints the sweet that ruins a diet.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich steamed sponge soaked in golden syrup, a classic British dessert that ruins any slimming plan.

clue.text: Award author Leon second in racing car

parts.note: a grant is a sum awarded
Leon Uris, American novelist of Exodus
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A prize for a novelist who comes second in a motor race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'author Leon' is Leon Uris; 'in' is only a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-performance touring sports car, the Italian phrase meaning grand touring.

clue.text: Drive home I see as tricky, maintaining a measure of speed

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold, so the rearranged letters hold the speed unit
tricky suggests something twisted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: mph, miles per hour

explanation.surface: Driving home, someone finds the route awkward while holding a steady speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges I SEE AS to EASISE, and 'maintaining' puts MPH inside it. 'Drive home' is not a journey but means stress a point.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive a point home is to stress it forcefully.

clue.text: Flipping scallywag is a music maker

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a rat is a rascal or scoundrel

explanation.surface: A cursing rascal who turns out to play an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild curse but turns RATIS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-necked Indian stringed instrument, plucked to make music.

clue.text: Conundrum: drug with a title in report?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: E, the drug ecstasy, given the title Mister

explanation.surface: A puzzle over a drug figure named in an official report.
explanation.walkthrough: E, slang for ecstasy, with the title Mr before it, is said MISTER E.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle or riddle that is hard to explain is an enigma.

clue.text: Silence soon enveloping northern river

parts.note: sh is the call for silence

indicators.note: the word for soon envelops the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: Quiet will soon settle over a river in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enveloping' puts N inside ANON.
explanation.definitionFit: The longest river in Ireland.
